solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suffering anguish from public school education (8)

blocks.note: Harrow is a famous English fee-paying school (in Britain a 'public school' is a private one)
ED is the standard abbreviation for education

annotation.surface: A former pupil still traumatised by the years at an elite boarding school.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface invites you to read 'public school education' as one idea; split it into the school and its abbreviation. HARROW is also the verb behind the answer, which makes the charade feel like a pun.
annotation.definitionFit: To be harrowed is to be deeply distressed, so it means suffering anguish.

clue.text: Architects primarily like skyscrapers in any shape or form (2,3)

indicators.note: what comes primarily is the first thing, so take the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Architects
skyscrapers are tall

annotation.surface: Architects who favour skyscrapers of every design.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In any shape or form' looks like a comment on building designs, but it is the idiom meaning 'whatsoever', as in 'not at all'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Not in any shape or form' and 'not at all' mean the same thing.

clue.text: Capital green space kept rangers busy (7,4)

indicators.note: busy letters are bustling about, out of their places

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A park in the capital where the rangers have a lot of work to do.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads straight through, with rangers naturally belonging in a park. Regent's Park is a large royal park in central London, the capital meant here.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: it is one of London's royal parks, and London is the capital.

clue.text: Horrible twerp regularly made a lasting impression? (8)

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of tWeRp
to etch is to cut a permanent mark

annotation.surface: An awful little twerp who nonetheless left a memorable mark.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: 'made a lasting impression' sounds like fame but is the literal act of etching.
annotation.definitionFit: Wretched can mean very bad or horrible, as in 'wretched weather'.

clue.text: Opposite of a sure thing (8,7)

blocks.note: take 'a' as the little word itself, a grammatical term, rather than meaning 'one'; its opposite is its partner word 'the'
the surface reading is a certainty, a bet that cannot lose; each word also has a synonym used in grammar

annotation.surface: Something that is anything but certain.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'the opposite of a certainty', pointing towards a gamble. Read 'a' as the word itself: its opposite is 'the', the definite article, and 'definite article' also means a sure thing.
annotation.definitionFit: The definite article, 'the', is the grammatical opposite of the indefinite 'a'.

clue.text: Lake bends around urban area (6)

indicators.note: turned around, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
wood that warps bends out of shape

annotation.surface: A lake whose shoreline curves round a town.
annotation.walkthrough: L and WARPS are put together first, then the whole LWARPS is turned around to give SPRAWL.
annotation.definitionFit: A sprawl is a large, spread-out built-up area, as in urban sprawl.

clue.text: Wooden top from table with durable exterior (6)

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter
SOLID forms the outside, so it wraps round the T

blocks.note: solid = durable, and it is the outside part
first letter of table, placed inside SOLID

annotation.surface: A wooden tabletop with a hard-wearing finish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wooden top' looks like a furniture phrase, but the definition is just 'Wooden', meaning expressionless, and 'top from table' is the T.
annotation.definitionFit: A stolid, wooden person shows little emotion or animation.

clue.text: Some very expensive whiskey (3)

indicators.note: some of the words, so a part of the phrase

blocks.note: inside veRY Expensive

annotation.surface: A pricey whiskey.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words: the end of 'very' and the start of 'expensive'.
annotation.definitionFit: Rye is a North American whiskey distilled from rye grain.

clue.text: Small piece required for board game evening? (9)

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for small
a knight is a chess piece

annotation.surface: A small counter needed for a night of board games.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a weeknight is one kind of evening. 'Board game evening' reads as one phrase, but the evening is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a weeknight is one particular kind of evening.

clue.text: Manipulate women’s point of view (6)

blocks.note: W = women, as on toilet doors; the possessive 's adds no letters
an angle on something is a point of view

annotation.surface: Twisting a female perspective to suit one's own ends.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive 's only joins women to the point of view; it adds no letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To wangle is to get or arrange something by crafty manipulation.

clue.text: Fewer old bananas produced blossoms (8)

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: An ageing banana plant that manages fewer flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the plant that blossoms, but it is the crazy-letters signal, and 'produced blossoms' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to flower is to produce blossoms, and the past tense matches.

clue.text: Covert agent abandoning the last course of action (4)

indicators.note: the agent gives up its last letter

blocks.note: a plant is a spy placed secretly in an organisation
PLANT without its last letter T

annotation.surface: A secret agent walking away from the final mission.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The last' looks like the last course of a meal or mission; it is the last letter of PLANT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a plan and a course of action are both a decided way forward.

clue.text: Soldiers controlling movements around the centre of Belgium (10)

indicators.note: CONTINENT wraps round the G
the central letter of the seven-letter Belgium

blocks.note: continent means having control of one's bowels, so controlling movements
middle letter of BelGium, placed inside CONTINENT

annotation.surface: Troops directing manoeuvres in the heart of Belgium.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Movements' sounds like troop movements, but here it means bowel movements: a continent person controls them.
annotation.definitionFit: A contingent is a body of troops forming part of a larger force.

clue.text: Poor child sputtering terribly and close to collapse (11)

indicators.note: done terribly, so the letters are jumbled
the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
last letter of collapsE, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A sickly child coughing badly and about to faint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to collapse' reads as 'nearly collapsing', but it gives just the final E of collapse to join the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A guttersnipe is a scruffy, poor child who lives on the streets.

clue.text: Opportunity for faction to seize power (8)

indicators.note: SECT seizes, that is holds, the P

blocks.note: pro = for, as in pros and cons
a sect is a faction or breakaway group
P = power in physics, placed inside SECT

annotation.surface: A chance for a political faction to take over the government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a mere link word, but here it is a piece of wordplay in its own right, and 'power' is placed inside the faction.
annotation.definitionFit: A prospect is a possibility or chance of something happening.

clue.text: Destruction of one old city upset people (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read upwards

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ur is the ancient city in Mesopotamia, the crossword's favourite old city
a nation is a people

annotation.surface: The sacking of an ancient city that distressed its inhabitants.
annotation.walkthrough: Ur, the ancient Mesopotamian city, is crossword shorthand for 'old city'. In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so only the one and the city are read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ruination is the state of being ruined, just as destruction is.

clue.text: Measure of warmth associated with a garment (4)

blocks.note: the tog is the British unit rating the warmth of duvets and clothing
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A warmth rating that comes attached to a piece of clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a clothing label; tog ratings are printed on British duvets.
annotation.definitionFit: A toga is the loose outer garment of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Type of clue featuring in extremely likeable game (8)

indicators.note: ACROSS features inside the other letters
at the extremes, so the first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of LikeablE, wrapped round ACROSS
crossword clues are across or down

annotation.surface: A kind of puzzle clue appearing in a very enjoyable pastime.
annotation.walkthrough: The self-reference is the trick: the 'type of clue' is ACROSS, the kind this down clue is not.
annotation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Musical performer keen to make a comeback (4)

indicators.note: coming back means travelling backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: avid = keen; the letters then run backwards

annotation.surface: A singer eager to return to the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a showbiz comeback story, which suits a diva perfectly.
annotation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female singer, especially in opera.

clue.text: A bad experience having knocked back too much booze (8)

indicators.note: knocked back puts OTT in reverse

blocks.note: used as it stands
a mare, short for nightmare, is British slang for a bad experience
OTT = over the top, too much

annotation.surface: A rough time after downing more drink than was wise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking, which the surface wants, but it is the instruction to turn OTT round.
annotation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur, so a kind of booze.

clue.text: Region inhabited by rook, duck and lorikeet? (6)

indicators.note: PART is lived in by R and O, so they go inside

blocks.note: a part of the country is a region
R = rook in chess notation
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

annotation.surface: A habitat home to three different birds.
annotation.walkthrough: Rook and duck look like fellow birds for the list, but they give letters; only the lorikeet, marked by '?' as an example, is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, marked by the question mark: lorikeets are small Australasian members of the parrot family.

clue.text: Challenging leader marks a test loosely (10)

indicators.note: arranged loosely, so not in their written order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A demanding teacher who grades an exam carelessly.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a strict teacher, which is the answer itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A taskmaster is a demanding boss who sets hard work.

clue.text: So, the final part of Sherlock is excellent! (4)

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: sic is Latin for 'so, thus'
last letter of SherlocK

annotation.surface: A fan declaring the last episode of the TV series Sherlock brilliant.
annotation.walkthrough: SIC is the word put in brackets after a quoted error to mean 'thus in the original'. Sick as praise is modern slang.
annotation.definitionFit: In youthful slang, sick means excellent, as in 'that was sick!'.

clue.text: Conservative/Labour split (5)

blocks.note: C = Conservative, the British party
the Labour Party is on the political left

annotation.surface: A political divide between Britain's two main parties.
annotation.walkthrough: The slash makes 'Conservative/Labour split' look like a headline about the two parties; the last word alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Cleft means split, as in a cleft chin or cleft rock.

clue.text: Famous hotel is ring-shaped (8)

blocks.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
used as it stands
a torus is a ring shape, so toric means ring-shaped

annotation.surface: A celebrated hotel built in a circle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Famous hotel' reads as one phrase, but the hotel is only H and 'Famous' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Historic means famous or important in history.

clue.text: Match that Napoli lose in the end (3)

indicators.note: take the end of each word

blocks.note: last letters of thaT napolI losE

annotation.surface: A football fixture that the Naples side eventually loses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'eventually', but it asks for the end letter of each of the three words before it. A tie is a knockout cup match in British football.
annotation.definitionFit: In British sport a tie is a match between two teams, as in a cup tie.

clue.text: Instrument position to cover bowler’s target (6)

indicators.note: SET covers PIN by going round it

blocks.note: to set something is to position it
a tenpin bowler aims at the pins; placed inside SET

annotation.surface: Placing an object to shield what a bowler is aiming at.
annotation.walkthrough: In a British clue 'bowler' usually means cricket, pointing at the stumps; here it is tenpin bowling.
annotation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Popular party is overrun (6)

blocks.note: what is in is popular
a fest is a festive gathering or party

annotation.surface: A popular party that runs on too late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overrun' looks like a party going over time, but it is the verb meaning swarmed over by pests.
annotation.definitionFit: To infest and to overrun both mean to swarm over a place in large numbers.

clue.text: What hosts large competition for one part of football team? (8)

indicators.note: EH hosts, that is holds, the other letters

blocks.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
L = large, as on clothes sizes
a sporting event is a competition; L and EVENT go inside EH

annotation.surface: A question about which club puts on a big tournament.
annotation.walkthrough: A football team has eleven players, so each is one eleventh of it; the question mark admits the definition is playful.
annotation.definitionFit: A football side has eleven players, so one player is an eleventh of the team.
